title: Docebo vs. Degreed: Enterprise learning platform comparison
summary: Docebo and Degreed both combine learning, skills, and AI. Compare their key differences, ideal use cases, pricing, and enterprise capabilities.
body_markdown:
You’re comparing Docebo vs. Degreed, and the old[learning management system (LMS) vs. learning experience platform (LXP)](https://www.docebo.com/learning-network/blog/lms-vs-lxp/) shorthand doesn’t settle it anymore. Both platforms now compete across learning, skills intelligence, and AI.


Degreed rolled out[Maestro](https://degreed.com/experience/blog/degreed-maestro-ai-purpose-built-for-learning/) , its AI coaching layer, with its July 2025 release, alongside Skills+ for skills-based development. Docebo acquired[365Talents](https://www.docebo.com/learning-network/blog/why-docebo-acquired-365talents/) on January 20, 2026, to power Docebo Skills Intelligence, then launched Docebo Knowledge and Docebo Agents on[October 28, 2026](https://www.docebo.com/company/newsroom/docebo-expands-workforce-readiness-platform-with-launch-of-knowledge-and-agents/) . The feature lists overlap more than ever. The platform strategies don’t.


- **Degreed** is an LXP-first platform built for[content discovery](https://degreed.com/experience/lxp/) , personalization, and skills-based development. **Docebo** is an AI workforce readiness platform built on an enterprise LMS foundation, with integrated skills intelligence through 365Talents.
- **Degreed** shines when you want a better learner experience across an ecosystem you already run. **Docebo** is a strong fit when you want to consolidate more learning operations and connect development to broader workforce needs.


This guide compares both across architecture, compliance, discovery, skills, AI, external training, integrations, implementation, and total cost of ownership (TCO). You’ll leave with one question to anchor your decision. Do you want to enhance your existing learning ecosystem, or consolidate more of your learning and workforce readiness into one platform?


## Docebo vs. Degreed at a glance


Evaluation criteria Docebo Degreed Ideal fit


**Overall platform breadth** Enterprise workforce readiness platform combining learning management, skills, and workforce development LXP-first platform centered on discovery and skills-based learning **Docebo** : Better for consolidating more of the learning lifecycle in one platform


**Learning management and compliance** Native LMS tools to assign and track structured training, certifications, and compliance requirements Supports structured learning and assignments, but formal administration isn’t its primary focus **Docebo** : Stronger when you must manage mandatory training and certification directly


**Learning discovery and experience** Personalized recommendations, content marketplace, and social learning inside the LMS Strong content aggregation and personalized, self-directed discovery across many sources **Degreed** : Better when the employee-facing experience is your top buying criterion


**Skills intelligence** Docebo Skills Intelligence, powered by 365Talents, connects skill gaps to workforce planning, internal mobility, and development Skills+ supports skills normalization, gap analysis, and personalized upskilling **Docebo** : Stronger when skills data must inform workforce decisions beyond learning


**AI learning and content creation** AI content creation, Roleplay, tutoring, knowledge access, and operational agents, plus a no-code builder for custom AI agents. Maestro is strong in AI coaching, practice, and personalized development Compare the specific workflows you need. **Docebo** spans content creation, learner practice, and administrative automation; **Degreed** emphasizes personalized development and practice.


**Customer and partner training** Runs employee learning alongside customer education and partner training Can deliver learning to customers, partners, suppliers, and other non-employees **Docebo** : Better when external training is a major use case next to employee learning


**Integrations and tech-stack strategy** APIs, SSO, HR information system (HRIS) connections, and platforms such as Workday and Salesforce, plus a consolidation path Designed to connect many learning and HR systems across an existing ecosystem **Degreed** : Stronger if you’re deliberately keeping a best-of-breed stack


**Pricing and TCO** Can cut cost and complexity by replacing overlapping learning tools Can enhance an incumbent LMS without replacing it **Docebo** : Stronger TCO story for consolidation; **Degreed** fits if your LMS stays


## When Docebo is the better fit


Docebo wins when you need one platform to run learning operations while connecting development to skills and workforce readiness.


**You need one platform for formal and self-directed learning:** Docebo pairs enterprise LMS infrastructure with personalized learning. Assigned courses and self-directed exploration live in one place. Your learners get one front door and your admins one back office, while Degreed is better at enhancing an ecosystem you already run.


**Compliance and certification are business-critical:** If a failed audit can stall your business, your learning platform has to act as the system of record. Docebo handles mandatory learning, SCORM and xAPI content, certification, recertification, compliance tracking, and[audit-ready reporting](https://www.docebo.com/solutions/compliance-training/) natively. Automate the reminders and prove completion on demand, so your compliance team stops chasing spreadsheets before every audit.


**You want skills intelligence to drive workforce decisions:** Docebo Skills Intelligence, powered by 365Talents and[sold as a separate product](https://www.docebo.com/products/skills-intelligence/) , infers skills from everyday work and learning signals. It keeps them current as roles change and connects that data to workforce planning, internal mobility, and talent development. For your chief HR officer, that means a defensible answer when the board asks whether your workforce is ready for AI.


**You train employees and external audiences:** Docebo’s[extended enterprise architecture](https://www.docebo.com/products/extended-enterprise/) runs separate environments for employees, customers, partners, and members. Each gets its own branding, content, and reporting. Run customer education and partner training alongside employee onboarding, and sell courses through ecommerce, from the same platform.


**You want to consolidate your learning technology:** Every extra platform adds an integration to maintain, a contract to renew, and an admin to train. In many enterprises, Degreed runs on top of a second learning system such as Workday Learning or Cornerstone. Docebo can replace both, bringing LMS, LXP-style discovery, skills, and content creation onto one platform with one admin experience and one set of learning data.


**You want AI to support learning and the work behind it:** Docebo combines AI content creation with Roleplay, tutoring, knowledge access, and workflow automation. Subject-matter experts can create learning content, employees can practice workplace scenarios, and learning teams can automate operational tasks. A[no-code agent builder](https://www.docebo.com/products/agents/) lets customers create custom AI agents tailored to their own workflows, while Model Context Protocol (MCP) connections bring Docebo capabilities into external AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot.


## When Degreed is the better fit


Degreed is the stronger choice when you already have established learning infrastructure and mainly want better discovery, personalization, and skills-based development.


**You already have an LMS you intend to keep:** Degreed adds a modern learning and skills experience on top of your core LMS. If that LMS handles compliance well and your contract has years left, Degreed improves the front end without a migration. You protect the investment you’ve made and still give employees a modern place to learn.


**Content aggregation is the main challenge:** Degreed is strong at pulling internal content and third-party libraries, such as LinkedIn Learning, into one experience. If your learners bounce between five catalogs, one search fixes a daily headache. One search across every source saves time and surfaces content people would otherwise never find.


**You prioritize employee-led learning:** Its LXP-first model suits self-directed learning and personalized development. Content recommendations, skill profiles, and Maestro coaching put employees in charge of their own upskilling. That works well in cultures where people already own their development.


**You prefer a best-of-breed ecosystem:** Degreed fits organizations that intentionally run several specialist systems and want a layer that connects them. If you chose that architecture on purpose, Degreed respects it. Just budget for the integrations that keep those systems talking.


## Docebo vs. Degreed: Detailed platform and capability breakdown


Both products overlap across learning, skills, and AI, so a feature checklist won’t separate them. Evaluate how each platform delivers those capabilities and what role it’ll play in your wider tech stack.


### Core platform architecture


**Degreed:** Degreed is built on the learning experience platform model, with discovery and skills-based development at the center. It’s designed to sit on top of the systems you already own.


**Docebo:** Docebo is built on an enterprise learning management system that handles content management, delivery, and administration. Skills Intelligence, Docebo Knowledge, and Docebo Agents extend that core into a closed loop: Detect skill gaps, deliver learning, and validate progress.


**Bottom line:** Degreed is stronger as an experience layer over an existing ecosystem. Docebo is stronger when you want one learning platform to own more of your operations.


### Learning management and compliance


**Degreed:** Degreed supports assignments and structured development, but it stays oriented around the learning experience. Formal administration usually remains with another system.


**Docebo:** Docebo provides native LMS infrastructure for compliance training, certifications, and SCORM and xAPI content. Automated compliance tracking and audit-ready reporting give you a clear record when auditors ask. That keeps compliance management inside your daily workflow.


**Bottom line:** Choose Docebo when the learning management system itself must act as your formal system of record.


### Learning discovery and experience


**Degreed:** Content aggregation, personalized discovery, and self-directed learning are core product strengths. Reviewers call it user-friendly, as the customer reviews below show.


**Docebo:** Docebo combines personalized content recommendations with a content marketplace, social learning, gamification, and leaderboards. Formal training sits in the same learning platform, so learners don’t switch tools to finish a required course. G2 reviewers often praise its ease of use and customization.


**Bottom line:** Degreed has the edge for discovery-first learning. Docebo is stronger when discovery has to coexist with formal learning management.


### Skills intelligence and workforce development


**Degreed:** Degreed uses skills intelligence through[Skills+](https://degreed.com/experience/skills/) to identify skill gaps and personalize upskilling. Maestro adds skill reviews, so employees can test and build capability inside the experience.


**Docebo:** Docebo Skills Intelligence, powered by 365Talents, infers skills from work signals, learning activity, and manager validation. It connects that living view to workforce planning, internal mobility, and talent development. Skill gaps trigger targeted learning, and progress is measured by capability.


**Bottom line:** Both have substantial skills capabilities. Degreed’s skills picture is closely tied to learning activity, skill ratings, and manager assessments. Docebo Skills Intelligence also draws on HRIS data, job descriptions, and projects, so it’s stronger when skills must inform workforce planning and internal mobility, not just course recommendations.


### AI capabilities and content creation


**Degreed:** Maestro,[Degreed’s AI layer](https://degreed.com/experience/artificial-intelligence/) , covers coaching, roleplay, skill reviews, and automated pathway curation. Its coaches retain past conversations, so guidance gets more personal over time.


**Docebo:** Docebo applies AI features across the learning workflow. Its AI authoring tool helps subject-matter experts turn expertise into courses faster, and personalized recommendations support adaptive learning paths. Docebo Agents act on tasks, Docebo Knowledge connects 20+ knowledge sources, and AI Tutor explains and summarizes content around the clock.


**Bottom line:** Docebo has the edge. Degreed’s AI story centers on coaching and practice. Docebo covers those with Roleplay and AI Tutor, then adds a no-code agent builder, so your team can automate the work behind any learning workflow itself instead of waiting on a vendor roadmap.


### Customer and partner training


**Degreed:** Degreed can also deliver learning to customers, partners, suppliers, and other non-employees. Public detail on how it separates and reports on those audiences is thinner, so ask to see your exact scenario.


**Docebo:** Docebo is built to run external training as its own program. Each audience gets a separate branded portal with its own content and reporting, ecommerce lets you sell courses, and headless delivery puts learning inside your own product or website.


**Bottom line:** Docebo is the stronger fit when customer or partner training is a substantial part of your learning strategy.


### Integrations and tech-stack strategy


**Degreed:** Degreed is designed to[orchestrate](https://developer.degreed.com/docs/degreed-integrations) learning across your existing HR, LMS, content, and collaboration systems. That’s its core job, and it does it well.


**Docebo:** Docebo supports 400+ enterprise integrations through APIs, SSO, and HRIS connections such as[Workday](https://www.docebo.com/integration/workday/) . It also connects to customer relationship management (CRM) tools like Salesforce and to business intelligence tools. And it gives you a clear path to retire overlapping tools.


**Bottom line:** Degreed is stronger for a best-of-breed strategy. Docebo is stronger when reducing platform fragmentation is a priority.


### Implementation and support


G2’s “Time to Implement” averages, drawn from user reviews, put Docebo at[4 months](https://www.g2.com/products/docebo/pricing) and Degreed at[5 months](https://www.g2.com/products/degreed/reviews) .


**Degreed:** Implementation depends heavily on integrations with your existing LMS, HRIS, and content ecosystem. Reviewers praise its customer service and third-party content integrations.


**Docebo:** Implementation depends on migration scope, learning workflows, audiences, and integrations. Focused rollouts can move fast. Multi-audience migrations take longer, so scope them early.


**Bottom line:** G2 data gives Docebo a slight edge on time to implement, but your existing stack and deployment scope will shape the effort more than the vendor you pick.


### Pricing and total cost of ownership


Neither vendor publishes pricing. Both use custom, quote-based enterprise pricing, so skip the per-user comparison and model total cost instead.


**Degreed:** Degreed adds learning experience and skills functionality while preserving your LMS investment. You’ll still pay for, integrate, and administer both systems.


**Docebo:** Docebo may lower TCO if you can retire overlapping learning tools and reduce integration complexity. Budget separately for Skills Intelligence, which is sold as its own product.


**Bottom line:** Docebo has the stronger TCO argument when consolidation is the goal. Degreed makes more sense when your incumbent LMS will stay.

## Which platform is the right choice for your team?


Choosing between Docebo and Degreed comes down to one thing. Do you want to add a skills-first learning experience to your existing ecosystem, or consolidate learning, skills, compliance, and workforce readiness into one platform? Use these seven questions to decide:


**Do you already have an LMS you intend to keep?** If yes, Degreed may be the stronger fit for adding discovery, personalization, and skills-based development.


**Do you need one platform to manage formal learning as well as personalized development?** If yes, Docebo is the stronger fit.


**Are compliance, certification, or mandatory training major requirements?** Docebo is better suited to managing these workflows inside the learning platform itself.


**Is content aggregation across many providers and systems your main priority?** Degreed has a strong advantage as an LXP and learning orchestration layer.


**Do skills need to support workforce planning, internal mobility, and broader talent decisions?** Docebo Skills Intelligence offers a stronger fit.


**Are customer, partner, or other external training programs important?** Docebo is better suited to complex extended enterprise learning.


**Is your strategy to consolidate learning technology or maintain a best-of-breed ecosystem?** Choose Docebo for consolidation and Degreed for keeping specialist systems connected.


Degreed is a strong choice if you have an established LMS and want better content discovery, personalized learning, and skills-based development across your ecosystem. Docebo is the stronger choice if you want a broader workforce readiness platform. It combines formal learning management, skills intelligence, compliance, workforce development, and external training in one place.

## FAQs


###


Degreed is a learning experience platform (LXP), not a learning management system. In many enterprises it runs alongside an LMS such as Workday Learning or Cornerstone, which handles assignments, compliance, and certification. Before you replace an LMS with Degreed, confirm it can handle the compliance, certification, and administration workflows you rely on.


###


Both connect to your HRIS and other enterprise tools through APIs and SSO, so employee, skills, and learning data move between systems. Docebo also offers connections to Workday and Salesforce, plus a path to consolidate tools.


###


Docebo is ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certified, GDPR-aligned, and hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS) with[encryption in transit and at rest](https://trust.docebo.com/faq) . Docebo Skills Intelligence, built in Europe by 365Talents, is GDPR-compliant by design and[ISO/IEC 42001 certified](https://365talents.com/en/resources/365talents-becomes-world-first-hrtech-certified-iso42001/) for responsible AI. Degreed holds SOC 2 Type II, TISAX, and[ISO 27001 (added March 2026)](https://degreed.com/experience/newsroom/degreed-achieves-iso-27001-and-iso-9001-certifications/) , so request current reports from both.


###


Alternatives include Cornerstone OnDemand for enterprise learning and talent management, Absorb LMS for enterprise and external learning, and 360Learning for collaborative learning. Others are Litmos for compliance-focused training, Moodle as an open-source LMS, and Workday Learning within a broader HR suite.
